title: Cartwise Shopper Payouts Catch-Up Limit for a Recently Replaced Destination
content:
**Cartwise Shopper Payouts — Payments Risk rule on catch-up deposits to a new destination**

**Clause 1 (the limit).** The catch-up limit for a recently replaced destination depends on how recently the destination was replaced and how long ago the account was verified:

(a) where the destination was replaced fewer than 30 days ago and the account was verified 12 or more whole months ago, the catch-up draws on at most the largest single weekly sweep deposit ever booked on the account, re-send deposits (those pointing to a returned-transfer entry) not counted;

(b) where the destination was replaced fewer than 30 days ago and the account was verified fewer than 12 whole months ago, it draws on at most a fixed 200.00 of the balance;

(c) otherwise it draws on the whole balance.

**Clause 2 (effect).** The catch-up deposit draws on the smaller of the balance on the account and the limit in Clause 1.

**Clause 3 (counting).** Days since the destination was replaced are counted in calendar days from the moment of the replacement (the destination change recorded on the account), or from the opening date of the account when the destination was never replaced, to the day of the catch-up. Months since verification are whole months from the account's verification date to the day of the catch-up.

## Decision table

| Destination replaced | Verified | Limit drawn on |
|---|---|---|
| Fewer than 30 days ago | 12 or more whole months ago | Largest single weekly sweep deposit ever booked (re-send deposits excluded) |
| Fewer than 30 days ago | Fewer than 12 whole months ago | 200.00 |
| 30 days ago or more | Any time | The whole balance |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Replaced 29 days ago: fewer than 30 days, so row (a) or (b) applies. Replaced exactly 30 days ago: not fewer than 30, so the whole balance is drawn on.
- Verified 11 whole months ago: fewer than 12, so 200.00. Verified exactly 12 whole months ago: 12 or more, so the largest single weekly sweep deposit.
- An account never replaced, opened 18 days ago: the count runs from the opening date, so it is fewer than 30 days.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A hypothetical account has a balance of 480.00. Its weekly sweep deposits have included 310.40 as the largest, and a re-send deposit of 350.00 pointing to a returned-transfer entry, which is not counted.
- Destination replaced 12 days ago, verified 20 whole months ago: the limit is 310.40, and the catch-up draws on the smaller of 480.00 and 310.40, that is 310.40.
- Destination replaced 12 days ago, verified 8 whole months ago: the limit is 200.00, so it draws on 200.00.
- Destination replaced 45 days ago: it draws on the whole 480.00.
- Balance of 150.00, destination replaced 5 days ago, verified 8 whole months ago: the smaller of 150.00 and 200.00 is 150.00.
